title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Tunnel Close Echo Architecture
purpose: Define the server-side helper boundary for reading WebSocket tunnel messages and echoing a received close frame on accepted RFC 9220 streams.
design_summary: The accepted tunnel context now owns one server-side WebSocket message reader and exposes message read/write helpers above the raw QUIC stream. `ReadMessageAsync` incrementally consumes client bytes using the trace-owned parser, buffers any additional complete messages, and returns null on clean stream completion. `WriteMessageAsync` formats unmasked server-to-client frames. `EchoCloseAsync` validates a received close frame with the close parser, writes the same close payload back as an unmasked server close frame, and completes the writable side of the tunnel stream.
data_and_state_considerations: Parser state is scoped to the accepted tunnel context so frame-split buffering and fragmented-message state remain isolated per request stream. The close echo helper does not close the QUIC connection and does not reset the stream; it uses the orderly stream FIN path after sending the WebSocket close frame.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Client frames remain subject to server-side masking validation through `Http3WebSocketMessageReader`.
Invalid close payloads are rejected before the helper writes an echo frame.
The server close frame is emitted unmasked, matching RFC 6455 endpoint-role rules.
The helper completes only the writable side after the echoed close frame so the tunnel uses orderly FIN rather than H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED.
risks: This slice proves close echo on the local server-handler path only; it does not claim a complete WebSocket API surface.
Live external WebSocket-over-H3 peer proof remains future work.
Application-specific close code selection beyond echoing a peer close payload remains handler policy.
